Ok I'll change it, thank you. What could I use to know about the already existing exercises? does it exist a section or a kind of list available somewhere?

The official way is to search the titles here:
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/community
(Change the filter from "Pending" to "Accepted" first. Some users said they couldn’t find that menu, so it seems that you’ve got to reach a certain condition before you gain access.)

Another, easier, way is to use the unofficial tool made by a fellow CodinGame player:
https://codingame.tools/

The third way is to write your own code to read and search CG's clash database.

Goal
* Consider adding a worked example to make the task easier to understand:

<<Example>>

Suppose [[R]] and [[M]] are:
```
CTACAAGCC
CTTCTCGCG
  ^ ^^  ^
```
The strands differ at the positions indicated by {{^}}.

For [[k]] = {{4}}, some contiguous windows are:
• CTAC vs CTTC => 1 mutation
• ACAA vs TCTC => 3 mutations
• AGCC vs CGCG => 2 mutations

After considering all possible windows of length {{4}}, the maximum number of mutations is 3, so the answer is 3.

Input & Output
* Please format all line numbers in <<bold>> (e.g. <<Line 1>>).

Cases
* Test 4: Please swap [[R]] and [[M]].

* Validator 4: Please swap [[R]] and [[M]].

* Please add a pair of cases where [[K]] = 1, and [[R]] and [[M]] share the same character at some, but not all, positions. The length of [[R]] and [[M]] should be around 30.

* Please add a pair of cases where the output is 0, and [[R]] and [[M]] consist of entirely random A/C/G/T characters. The length of [[R]] and [[M]] should be around 30.

* Please add 3 new pairs of cases in which the window for the maximum number of mutations is at different positions:

  • Pair 1: starts around the middle of the strands.

  • Pair 2: is not the final window but is near the end of the strands.

  • Pair 3: is the final window.

  I've generated some cases that you can use directly; they're available here: https://pastebin.com/KQD1raBb
  
  You're also welcome to generate your own cases instead, but please keep them similar in style to the ones I've provided (i.e. large [[K]] values + long and randomised strands).

Thanks.
"Some users said they couldn’t find that menu", yep I'm from those too. I'll use the other tools you mentioned. Thank you 😁

Glad to help!

Please note that two of the scenarios mentioned from my previous comment are missing. Please add them as Pairs 6 and 7, and renumber the existing Pairs 6, 7, 8 to 8, 9 and 10 respectively.
